causal_analysis.finding: The request omitted landUseType. The handler turns a missing query value into undefined; the service appends MISSING_LAND_USE_TYPE. Management constructs a query only when its landUseType state is truthy. This explains the eligibility response without asserting when or why that state failed to retain FOREST.

Dimension T contains exactly terrain.slopePercent and supplement.landUseType. Both are required, and each dimension needs at least two included values. Missing landUseType therefore makes T insufficient even with valid slope; the service projects evaluator insufficiency as INSUFFICIENT_DIMENSION. The two observed reasons can arise from the same omitted supplement. They do not independently establish a fixture or science defect.

Fixture payload explicitly sets terrain.slopePercent=45. Runner creates distinct OWNER/ADMIN/incompatible collections with confirmedAt and the same measurement payload, measurement version ihfr-measurement-v1. Eligibility checks confirmedAt presence, not age, and does not take observedAt. No DB state was queried by this agent. Generic INSUFFICIENT_DIMENSION alone cannot exclude other dimensions, but missing land use is sufficient to produce it.

Fixed first case waits for observable desktop record-before-reading composition, fills once, asserts FOREST and exact observedAt, captures first matching eligibility GET, and asserts contextual path/query before ELIGIBLE. OWNER/ADMIN block is byte-identical F3/F4: it fills once before viewport helpers, without composition precondition or initial expected-value assertions. Its failure cannot be attributed to edits in that block.

inspectUI044DetailMatrix captures current field values and requires equality through its loop, not FOREST plus the intended date. A baseline already missing land use can satisfy those assertions. Its final 1280x900 reset occurs after the loop field comparisons. inspectManagementViewports also snapshots current values; its explicit value checks occur in the 1440-to-375 resize with dialog open. Neither helper proves the desired values at caller entry or after return.

No explicit field setter was found in the inspected viewport helpers or cancel handler. closeConfirmation only closes confirmation and restores trigger focus. prepare(DIAGNOSE) validates observedAt but does not require landUseType; successful opening/canceling cannot establish FOREST. Dialog text does not display the values. These facts do not exclude an indirect lifecycle or controlled-input defect.

An input interaction before initial client composition, controlled state not being updated by that interaction, or a subsequent layout transition could explain the omitted value. F4 lacks field-value observations at the necessary boundaries to choose among them. The first-case repair passing is supporting contrast, not proof that OWNER encountered the same initial hydration mechanism. Product root cause is not established.
